title: Versioned availability cache for hotel bookings
name: Hotel availability cache

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code invalidates cached availability after reservations or price changes? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: There is no defect. Every write path (reserve and updatePrice) commits to the repository first and then bumps the hotel's version counter. Readers build the data key from the version they read, so after the INCR every reader uses a new key and the old entries become unreachable; they expire via the 300s TTL. A reader that read the old version before the bump and then fills the cache writes under the old version key, which no later reader looks at, so a slow fill cannot resurrect stale data under the current key. Failed reservations never reach invalidateHotel, which is fine because nothing changed. quote() is only an estimate: the authoritative check happens in decrementRooms.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why does invalidateHotel increment a counter instead of deleting the cached keys?
choices: DEL is not supported by ioredis for string keys
Incrementing also refreshes the TTL of every cached day
It invalidates every date for the hotel in one atomic command without knowing which date keys exist
It makes the cache write-through instead of cache-aside
choiceQuestions.explanation: Data keys embed the version, so one INCR on avail-ver:<hotel> makes all of that hotel's date keys unreachable at once, with no need to enumerate or SCAN dates. INCR does not touch TTLs of other keys, ioredis supports DEL fine, and reads still populate the cache lazily (cache-aside).

choiceQuestions.prompt: A get() call reads version 4, then misses and starts loading from the repo. Meanwhile a reservation commits and bumps the version to 5. The get() then writes its result. What does the next get() for that date see?
choices: It misses under version 5 and loads fresh data from the repo
It hits the entry just written and returns pre-reservation availability
It hits the entry just written, but the entry has the post-reservation data
It throws, because the version changed during the fill
choiceQuestions.explanation: The slow fill writes to avail:<hotel>:<date>:v4. The next get() reads version 5 and looks up the v5 key, which does not exist, so it loads from the repo. The v4 entry is orphaned and expires. Nothing in get() detects version changes or throws.

choiceQuestions.prompt: What is the main cost of this invalidation scheme under a hotel with heavy booking traffic?
choices: Old versioned entries are never removed and leak memory forever
Every reservation drops the cache for all dates of that hotel, lowering the hit rate and sending more reads to the repo
Each read needs a SCAN over all keys of the hotel
Reservations block until all readers finish
choiceQuestions.explanation: invalidateHotel bumps a hotel-wide version, so one booking for one night invalidates every cached date for that hotel. With frequent bookings, most reads miss. Orphaned entries do expire because each set uses EX 300. Reads use direct GETs, not SCAN, and nothing makes writes wait for readers.
